metadata.note: The Phillips and Rangeley Railroad (Phillips - Rangeley, 1891), a 2 ft gauge steam lumber and resort road in Franklin County, Maine, worked in through service with the Sandy River Railroad to Farmington, sold at auction to the Sandy River and Rangeley Lakes Railroad in June 1908, and dismantled 1934-35. Drawn from research/branches/phillips_and_rangeley_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), 2026-10-14; only the main line and the confirmed SR&RL years of the Rangeley Lake House (Marbles) extension are drawn. Rule 4 split at the 1908 sale: the P&R and SR&RL Phillips - Rangeley features share identical geometry.
sources: https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/mainerrs.pdf (Fowler, Maine line 41 'SRRL ex Phillips & Rangeley RR Phillips to Marbles'; z = 1894 Pathfinder, p6 = 1900 Pathfinder, q = 1904 TT, a = 1910 PTT, b = 1921 PTT, c = 1930 ticket list)
https://archive.org/details/annualreportrai11commgoog (Maine Railroad Commissioners' Report 1898, P&R return pp.173-181)
metadata.colour_note: Phillips and Rangeley Railroad colour #22B61E is new (checked programmatically against every colour in data/). Sandy River and Rangeley Lakes Railroad colour #6B4E9B is pulled from franklin_and_megantic_railway.geojson, where it was introduced.
source_conflicts: P&R -> SR&RL transfer: auction 12 Jun 1908 (Crittenden 1966 p.134 via Wikipedia) vs 'acquired' 30 Jun 1908 (Nashua City Station, ICC 1926). Either way mid-1908; split drawn P&R to 1907, SR&RL from 1908, matching the F&M/SR&RL split.
P&R incorporation: 12 Mar 1889 (ICC 1926 via Nashua City Station) vs 'date of organization April 17, 1889' (the company's own 1898 return). Does not affect drawn years.
P&R length: 28.6 mi (Fowler, Jones) vs 28.5 (srrl-rr.org) vs 28 (Wikipedia infobox).
Marbles extension length: 1700 ft (Wikipedia P&R) vs 0.5 mi (Fowler MP 46.7-47.2); OSM and OHM also disagree on its alignment (see the feature's geometry_quality).
Perham Junction - Barnjum: 'a 4-mile freight branch' (Wikipedia SR&RL, Jones 1980 p.237) vs Perham and Barnjum on Fowler's 1930 ticket list. Not drawn.
not_yet_sourced: END 1931, srrl-phillips-rangeley: rests on one Wikipedia paragraph (last steam train May 1931, railcar service north of Phillips ended autumn 1931) whose footnotes (Jones 1980 p.237 before, Crittenden 1966 pp.185-189 after) leave its exact source uncertain. Primary-type evidence stops at the 1930 ticket list. Check Crittenden 1966 or Jones 1980 directly, or a Chronicling America 'last train to Rangeley' story.
OPEN BOTH ENDS, srrl-rangeley-marbles: drawn 1910-1921 (the two timetables that list Marbles); real service lay somewhere within 1908-1927.

OMITTED: P&R-era Marbles extension 1906-1907. Its 1906 opening rests on a single uncited Wikipedia sentence and no P&R timetable listing Marbles was seen. Add a P&R feature on the srrl-rangeley-marbles geometry if a 1906 or 1907 timetable shows Marbles, and move the SR&RL start back if one shows it in 1908-1909.

OMITTED: SR&RL Madrid Junction - Number Six (Fowler line 43) and Madrid Junction - Madrid Village - 'Sandy River' (Fowler line 44). The only passenger evidence is the 1930 ticket list (a 1930 [ANCHOR] at most); both are absent from the 1910 and 1921 public timetables, and the branch layout (where the two legs forked, which is the 1902 Madrid Railroad) is unresolved.

OMITTED: Eustis Railroad (Eustis Junction - 'Green Farm'), leased to and run by the P&R, summer passenger service c.1905-1907/08 per uncited Wikipedia sentences. Green Farm is not located, so the passenger section cannot be drawn; do not draw the whole branch to Langtown on this evidence.
Who was the P&R's receiver 1905-1908, and did the Sandy River RR (the bondholder) work the P&R before the 1908 sale? If so the ownership split would move earlier.
The 'Kennebago Railroad' on the P&R's 1898 balance sheet is unidentified; no track found.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.

Not read directly: Crittenden 1966/1976, Jones 1979/1980, ICC 1926 valuation report, any primary timetable; attributions are via Wikipedia, Nashua City Station and Fowler. The 1898 and 1900 Maine Railroad Commissioners' returns were read (OCR).
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing drawn for freight-only years. Not drawn: the Madrid Railroad (Madrid Jct - Number Six) in the P&R era 1902/03-1908, a log feeder with no passenger evidence; the Eustis branch after 1908 (passenger service ended 1908, a pulpwood branch thereafter, the 3 mi beyond Langtown last used 1919); Perham Junction - Barnjum (built 1912-17, described as a freight branch, Oxford Paper pulpwood from 1928); the mill spurs at Redington, Sanders, Reed's and the Madrid Junction (Berlin Mills) mill; and 1932-35 (no service on the former P&R; the 1933-35 restart ran Carrabasset - Strong - Farmington only).
metadata.horsecar_audit: None: steam from the first trains (P&R #1, Portland Co. 1890).
metadata.line_label_audit: Labels written to the Rule 6 pattern at creation.
metadata.interurban_audit: Not interurban: a steam narrow-gauge common carrier, drawn intercity_rail (as franklin_and_megantic_railway.geojson).

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror): the ways tagged old_railway_operator='Sandy River & Rangeley Lakes Railroad' (gauge 610) west of Phillips - mapped as the grade itself or as the roads and snowmobile trail laid on it (Railroad Road, Fish Hatchery Road, Redington Road, Snowmobile ITS 89, Depot Street, Snowmobile Rangeley Downtown trail) - plus two SR&RL-named ways without the operator tag (451275845/1050910969, the Phillips museum track, and 183137447, the Marbles stub). Traced with opstrace.py (layered-DP router, operator ways 1x); every waypoint hand-pinned onto the grade because Nominatim returned township centroids for Phillips, Madrid and Rangeley and a different Redington (a Carrabassett Valley hamlet ~20 mi east). Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals. Cross-checked against OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) ways 201882134, 201882316 and 201882164 (operator 'Phillips and Rangeley Railroad', USGS topo + 3DEP); OHM used only as a check, never for dates. The Barnjum, Madrid and Eustis branch grades in the same tag set are excluded.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced: 28.39 mi against the documented 28.6 mi (Fowler Maine line 41 MP 18.1-46.7; Jones 1979 via Wikipedia, Rangeley MP 28.6; srrl-rr.org 28.5; infobox 28) - 0.7% short. No straight-line legs: 100% on OSM ways (28.0 mi old_railway_operator-tagged SR&RL, 0.4 mi SR&RL-named museum track at Phillips). Phillips end at 44.82326, -70.34249, on the grade 10 m from the OSM 'Phillips SR&RL station' building (way 703410916, 15 Depot Street), taken as P&R milepost 0 because the P&R's own mileposts check against it (measured on the unsimplified trace): Madrid Junction 5.2 traced vs 5.4, Perham Junction 10.1 vs 10.2, Redington Road east end 16.2 vs Redington 16.2, Eustis Junction (the OHM Eustis Railroad fork) 22.4 vs 22.4. OHM marks the 1879 Sandy River / 1891 P&R track boundary ~0.3 mi further east, at 44.8212, -70.3374 on Salmon Hole Road, between the station and the 1879 Sandy River bridge; no feature in data/ ends at Phillips yet (the Sandy River Railroad proper is not drawn), so whoever draws it should end it at this station point. Rangeley end at 44.96234, -70.63680, where the SR&RL-tagged trail way 1011701914 meets the lake-shore stub: traced 28.44 from the station vs MP 28.6, so the real Rangeley station may sit up to ~0.15 mi further west, on the stub drawn as the Marbles extension. Agrees with the OHM P&R ways to a median 3 m, max ~90 m (the last 0.2 mi into Rangeley, where OSM's trail and OHM's line part slightly). The line was lifted 1934-35; this is its own (only) alignment, not a later one.

segments.note: 2 ft gauge steam road from the Sandy River Railroad at Phillips over Sluice Hill (summit at Redington) to Rangeley. First train reached Redington 11 Oct 1890; regular service to Redington from Feb 1891; rails reached Rangeley 10 Jun 1891 and scheduled Rangeley - Farmington service began 1 Jul 1891 (Wikipedia P&R, from Crittenden/Jones; not individually footnoted). Passenger service confirmed by the 1894 Pathfinder (Fowler 'z': Phillips, Madrid, Redington Mills, Reed's Mill, Sander's Mill, Dead River, Rangeley as terminus) and by the company's own return for the year to 30 Jun 1898 (10,196 revenue passengers) and 1900. Trains ran through over the Sandy River Railroad to Farmington, but the P&R owned and worked its own line and equipment, so the through running is not a change of operator; neither is the receivership from 1905. Ends 1907: the line was sold at auction to the Sandy River & Rangeley Lakes on 12 Jun 1908 (Crittenden 1966 p.134 via Wikipedia; 'acquired' 30 Jun 1908 per ICC 1926), so 1908 goes to the SR&RL feature. Headway 720 (about two trains a day each way) is an ESTIMATE: srrl-rr.org's 'three round trips daily' Farmington - Rangeley is undated and likely summer-only, and no year-specific frequency was read (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: 1891 opening and 1908 sale from Wikipedia (Crittenden 1966/1976, Jones 1979/1980) and Nashua City Station (ICC 1926); passenger service from Fowler's 1894 Pathfinder letters and the P&R's own 1898 and 1900 returns to the Maine Railroad Commissioners. Headway and speed estimated.

segments.note: Former P&R, operated by the Sandy River & Rangeley Lakes from its June 1908 auction purchase (the P&R was NOT part of the 30 Jan 1908 Sandy River / F&M / K&DR consolidation). Rangeley, Redington, Dead River, Madrid and Phillips are in the 1910 and 1921 public timetables and on the 1930 ticket list (Fowler 'abc'), with Rangeley the terminus in 1930. Maine Central stock control 1911/12-1923 and the receivership from 8 Jul 1923 did not change the operating company. Seasonal gaps not shown at year granularity: no winter service 15 Dec 1922 - 1 May 1923, and no winter service north of Phillips December-May in each winter 1924-25 to 1928-29 (Crittenden 1966 pp.175-178; Jones 1980); gasoline railcars carried summer passengers from 1925. END 1931 RESTS ON ONE WIKIPEDIA PARAGRAPH: 'the last steam train left Rangeley in May 1931 and railcar service ... ended in the autumn of 1931', footnoted ambiguously to Jones 1980 p.237 and Crittenden 1966 pp.185-189, neither read directly. Primary-type evidence stops at the 1930 ticket list. All SR&RL service was suspended 8 Jul 1932 and the 1933-35 restart did not use this line (dismantled from summer 1934). Headway 720 is an ESTIMATE; no year-specific frequency was read (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: June 1908 purchase from Wikipedia (Crittenden 1966 p.134) and Nashua City Station (ICC 1926); 1910/1921 timetable and 1930 ticket listings from Fowler; 1931 end from one Wikipedia paragraph (Crittenden 1966 / Jones 1980, not read directly). Headway and speed estimated.

Drawn on OSM way 183137447 (railway=abandoned, gauge 610, named 'Sandy River & Rangeley Lakes Railroad', no operator tag) from 44.96234, -70.63680 to its end on the lake shore at 44.96102, -70.64145. No straight-line legs. OHM's P&R way 201882164 instead runs due west ~100 m further north to 44.96223, -70.64509 (0.41 mi), which would fit the documented length better; the two disagree on where the Rangeley Lake House station stood, and the shortfall may also be because Rangeley station itself lay west of the drawn Rangeley point (see the Phillips - Rangeley feature). Rails lifted 1927; its own alignment, not a later one.

segments.note: The Rangeley Lake House extension: end of track carried past Rangeley station to a small stone lake-shore station ('Marbles') for the hotel's guests, almost certainly summer-only. Drawn only for its CONFIRMED years: Marbles is in the 1910 and 1921 SR&RL public timetables (Fowler 'ab') and not on the 1930 ticket list, where Rangeley is the terminus. Both ends are withheld unknowns, not known dates: the SR&RL held it from June 1908, and rails were removed in 1927 'from the P&R extension formerly serving the Rangeley Lake House' (Crittenden 1966 p.183 via Wikipedia), so service lay somewhere within 1908-1927. Do not widen without a timetable. The extension's 1906-07 P&R years are omitted (single uncited sentence). Headway 720 is an ESTIMATE (Rule 3).
